aldemar.headline: The AI bill lands on Alphabet, the war premium holds — and CPI decides at 14:30
aldemar.standfirst: Tuesday's tape slipped quietly — S&P −0.32%, Nasdaq −0.60% — but the moves that matter were underneath: Alphabet fell 3.6% after closing a $25 billion bond deal to fund AI datacenters with free cash flow already negative, and crude added another 1.3% to 83.20 as Iran insisted the Strait of Hormuz "will not open until the US changes its behaviour" even while Pakistan shuttles between the sides saying a deal is close. Everything now waits on one number: CPI at 08:30 ET (14:30 Rome), the tightest gate holding the current regime call alive.

positions.title: Nothing open — nothing to track
positions.note: The book is flat, so there is no name-specific news to filter today. The moment a position opens, its wire gets tracked here.

themes.title: Pakistan says a deal is close — the strait says otherwise

items.html: Pakistan's interior minister in Tehran; Islamabad says the US and Iran are "close to a peace arrangement or a deal". A third mediator now works alongside Oman. Deal odds are the entire oil trade at the moment — this is the headline channel that would unwind the premium fastest.

Trump claims the strait is "open" under "100% control" and repeats the compensation demand; Iran's Rezaei says Hormuz "will not open until the US changes its behaviour". Both positions cannot be true, and tankers are pricing Tehran's version. Compensation demands on both sides are now the visible sticking point in otherwise-advancing talks.

Houthis hit a commercial vessel in the Bab al-Mandeb; casualties reported. The southern chokepoint stays live even while Hormuz negotiates, and Aramco's 400k-bpd Jazan refinery remains down after Sunday's strike. War-risk insurance and freight stay bid — a products-supply problem, not just a crude one.

WTI +1.30% to 83.20 — second day of the premium rebuilding. Follow-through after Monday's 5% jump rather than a reversal. Energy is where the war meets the CPI path, which is why today's print carries more than its usual weight.

themes.note: The transmission into your screens is oil → CPI → the regime call. Policy tightening's tightest gate is CPI y/y at 3.46 against the 2.5 floor, and two days of rebuilding crude premium hold that gate open. The reversal risk runs through a single headline — a signed Hormuz deal — which would hit oil, gold and the war hedge complex at once. Watch the talks, not the strikes.

world.title: Tech pays for its AI bill while the tape holds its breath for CPI

items.html: S&P −0.32%, Nasdaq −0.60%; VIX eases to 15.28 into the print. Rotation out of high-valuation growth into defensives, led by Alphabet's 3.6% drop — but a VIX easing on a down day says positioning ahead of CPI, not fear.

The AI capex race gets marked to market — Alphabet's $25B debt raise is the template. Negative free cash flow funded with 40-year paper reframes the hyperscaler build-out from strength to cost. Watch the read-across: the same question lands on every megacap with a datacenter bill.

Gold adds +0.49% to 4,383 — third green session. The war hedge and the soft-jobs disinflation bet feed the same trade. Gold refusing to give back Friday's two-sigma jump is the quiet confirmation that hedges are staying on through the print.

aldemar.ondeck: CPI release today — 08:30 ET. The regime's tightest gate is CPI y/y.

positions.title: 1 signal on GOOG — read before the open

items.html: GOOG — GOOG −3.6% as the AI bill comes due: $25B bond deal, negative free cash flow, DeepMind exits. The capex story stopped being an abstraction — quarterly capex hit $44.9B (+100% y/y), free cash flow went negative for the first time, and a $25B senior-notes deal (maturities out to 2066) closed Monday to keep funding datacenters, with DeepMind's executive turnover deepening the same day. The market has started charging for AI spending instead of rewarding it, and the stock confirmed at roughly two sigma; at 343.00 you are still +5.3% on entry with the stop 12.2% below — the news argues against adding, not against holding.
GOOG — Pixel 11 debut coverage builds. Product-cycle color with no number attached. Hardware launches do not move a $4.2T thesis.

positions.note: Signal changes the thesis, the levels or the size — earnings, a regulator with teeth, M&A, a ruling with a revenue line attached. Everything else is filed as noise on purpose; a real signal survives skepticism.
